target_customer: Owners of short-term rental properties such as Airbnbs who want to outsource management
problem: Traditional short-term rental managers charge 20 to 35 percent of revenue and rely on many local staff; owners want lower fees and less hassle.
business_model: Full-service property management for a flat percentage of booking revenue (website states 10 percent), with AI agents running operations and local operators supervising

founders.name: Edmond Niu
founders.background_notes: Duke roommate of the other founder per YC page.

founders.name: Shaan
founders.background_notes: YC page does not list a last name; research at Yale (brain computer interface) and Duke (computer architecture) per YC page. A search summary gave the surname Yadav, unverified.

competitors.name: Guesty
competitors.what: Short-term rental software adding AI agents for revenue management and replies
competitors.traction_then: AI revenue agent Dec 2025, ReplyAI Autopilot Apr 2026

competitors.name: Beenstay
competitors.what: AI-powered short-term rental management pitching 5 percent fees

competitors.name: ProhostAI
competitors.what: AI employees for property management and hospitality (YC S24)

competitors.name: Trellis
competitors.what: Autonomous agents for short-term rentals (YC launch)

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrates listing, messaging and pricing tools with LLM agents; the hard part is operations (cleaners, maintenance) not software.

defensibility.rationale: Several AI management entrants and incumbent PMS vendors offer similar agents; local operations and a fee advantage are the only differentiators.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Guesty and Hostaway shipped AI agents during 2025 and 2026; no acquisition of Atlia reported.

market_need_then: Owners complain about 20 to 35 percent management fees (company claim); the company reports managing about 80 properties at batch time.

branding.domain_note: Uses atlia.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.visual_style: Premium hospitality imagery, night time property hero

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand found; a different company holds the ATLIA trademark in games (Class 28), suggesting possible conflict.

outcome_analysis: Atlia is a two person Summer 2026 company at the earliest stage, with about 80 managed properties reported at batch time and no exit. Its fee advantage is easy for crowded AI property management rivals and incumbents to match, so it must prove unit economics from real operations, which is why no success or failure factors are assigned yet.
notes: No funding found beyond YC. Dealroom lists a $125k seed with locked details; unverified. Fee claims conflict across sources (10 percent flat on site; others say 10 to 30 percent more owner revenue). Website claims 10 percent flat fee.
